If you dont connect with the people where you are then you're free to find a new place. And you should think about what you enjoy and look for ways to connect with other people who enjoy those same things. You need to widen your experience with people. In fact the fastest way to overcome your shyness is to just talk to people in ordinary situations. In the grocery store or whatever, be friendly with the people. Most of them are bored and 99% of customers don't make their day interesting by ever saying anything.

Also, you may not have some condition like Aspergers, when I went to school I don't think I knew of anyone who was labelled in that way. I'm not even sure if that condition was ever talked about or if it even existed. I know that some people who had severe versions of it were in special schools but this was more because they were very extreme. There were some kids who were a bit more bookish and less social, and in fact one of my best friends definitely fitted that description. He's the reason I became so good with computers. By his mid 20's he'd completely overcome his 'nervousness'. Same goes with my wife in fact. She was extremely timid as a kid all the way until she was about 20-23 and then she made the effort to be more self assured and this was how I met her.

You don't need to fit in with other people, you just need to find a few people that genuinely like you. Maybe people that aren't like you but who you get on with. Accept invitations. You don't need a lot of friends. It's good to have people to hang out with, especially at weekends and stuff, but these people on facebook with 1500 'friends' are really kidding themselves. (also, fuck facebook, get rid of that bullshit)

thinking about it now.. I was a fairly insecure kid but nobody would have realised I think. it's hard to remember. I'm definitely 100 times more confident now but part of that comes with age. Partly because I lost my fear of adults. Most of my experience with adults growing up was with teachers. Older people don't really expect younger people to talk to them so they have a different 'register' for such conversations.

ah fuck it, I'm rambling.

anyway - here' s more general advice....

Youth hostels are EXCELLENT for meeting people. Staying in them or working in them. If you talk to someone and they're not very friendly then forget them. Dont let your experience with 1 arsehole stop you from being friendly with other people. And don't bear grudges, you have no idea what their life is like. Sometimes people are just not in the mood. It's no big deal. Avoid confrontations. You dont' want to know people like that anyway. Same goes for all people. Dont' waste your time with people who aren't fair to you.

And read some books. Not just novels. factual books about real events or people. Dont watch TV. It's complete poison. Become excellent at something you find interesting. You can learn the basics of anything on youtube now. And lookup the dictionary for words you don't know. I spent years guessing what words meant based on context. And ask questions if you're not sure about stuff. Take a moment to think about things and if you dont have a clue, then ask. People will think you're bright for asking the right question instead of pretending you know it all already. They probably know you should be asking questions so if you don't then they'll be less inclined to waste their time on you. People like good questions. It shows you're thinking.

If you're looking for something interesting to learn about then getting a psychology 101 textbook and read it. I was forced to take an elective subject first year of uni and I chose Psychology. I found it utterly fascinating. Broaden your interests and see what you like.

Also, you dont need to put yourself massively in debt to go to college just to meet some people. A good job with people you like and a few years will bring you friends. Just the fact that you want friends means you'll find them. And they'll find you. But I'm not going to tell you not to go to college if there's something you want to do which REQUIRES a degree or certificate. Then it's good.

Ok that's enough from me.. I have no idea if any of this really answers your questions.. but I hope some its helpful anyway
